History of Genetic ID
Genetic ID was the first commercial laboratory to test
for genetically modified organisms (GMOs) in crops
and food products. Since its inception in the summer of
1996, Genetic ID has built on its reputation as the most
accurate and reliable GMO testing laboratory,
becoming the only GMO lab that operates on five
continents, and the only one that offers systematic non-
GMO certification.
The Problem
In the spring of 1996, on a European lecture tour,
molecular biologist John Fagan realized that the
powerful biotech momentum to genetically engineer the
world's food supply was being challenged by rapidly
increasing consumer resistance. This posed a serious
problem for the food industry. Farmers, shippers and
manufacturers who wished to respond to consumer
demand for non-GMO food now needed reliable tests to
demonstrate the GMO content of their crops and food
products. Without such tests, they could not assure
their customers of the non-GMO foods they demanded.
At that time, many experts were saying that no
scientific test could detect GMOs in the food supply. If
true, this would have meant that governments could not
regulate and label GMO food, and the food índustry
could not respond to the wishes of their customers. Dr.
Fagan, however, had 17 years of experience conducting
DNA-level research for the National Institutes of
Health. He knew that DNA tests could detect GMO
crops and food products with a high degree of
sensitivity and reliability.
